chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Umar ibn Ali, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Umar, from Ibn Udhaynah who said, 'I heard Umar ibn Yazeed saying, 'Ma'rouf ibn Kharbouz narrated to me from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him)'

'He used to say: Woe to his mother, a sinner, who does not cease to be argumentative; woe to his mother, an immoral one, who does not cease to dispute; woe to his mother, a sinner, who speaks much regarding other than Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'

key_terms.آثِماً: A sinner, one who accumulates sins through actions.
key_terms.غَيْرِ ذَاتِ اللَّهِ: Other than Allah, referring to worldly matters or non-divine topics.
key_terms.فَاسِقاً: A sinner, one who transgresses divine boundaries.
key_terms.مُخَاصِماً: One who engages in constant conflict or quarreling.
key_terms.مُمَارِئاً: One who is argumentative or disputes persistently.
key_terms.وَيْلٌ: Woe or misery, a cry of lamentation often used in hadith to denote sorrow or punishment.

ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics of a sinner that bring woe to his mother according to Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual consequences of specific character flaws, linking persistent argumentativeness (mumar'ah), constant disputing (mukhasimah), and excessive idle talk (kur al-kalam) to the sorrow of the 'mother' (a term of endearment or reference to the soul's origin). It reflects the Shia emphasis on refining speech and conduct as acts of worship, warning that verbosity in non-divine matters dilutes spiritual presence.

en.hubeali: H 15034 – A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Umar Bin Ali, from his uncle Muhammad Bin Umar, from Ibn Azina who said, ‘I heard Umar Bin Yazeed saying, ‘Narrated to me Ma’rouf Bin Kharbouz, who has said:

‘Ali Bin Al-Husaynasws was saying: ‘Woe be unto a mother who defends the one who does not cease to sin! Woe be unto a mother of an immoral one who does not cease to dispute! Woe be unto a mother of a sinner, one who speaks a lot regarding other than Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic!’
en.sarwar: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, together, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Aban Bin Usman, from Al-Hassan Bin Umarat, from Nueym Al-Qazy, who has said: ‘Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said: ‘One morning, Ibrahim (as) saw a white hair in his (as) beard, so he (as) said: ‘The Praise is due to Allah (azwj), the Lord (azwj) of the Worlds Who (azwj) Made me reach to this age, and I (as) never disobeyed Allah (azwj) even for the blink of an eye’.
